html:
The passage of the Indian board game chaturanga to Sasanian Persia in the 6th century, where it became chatrang. This is the step that set chess on its way west.

A Middle Persian text, the Explanation of Chess, tells how an Indian king sent the game to the court of Khosrow I as a challenge, and how the Persian minister worked it out and answered with backgammon. The story is a legend, but it shows the game was known at the Sasanian court by about 600.

After the Arab conquest of Persia the game became shatranj, a favourite at the court of the Abbasid Caliphate, where players wrote the first books of chess problems. Muslim lands carried it on to Europe through Al-Andalus and the Emirate of Sicily. Persian words stayed in the game: "checkmate" comes from shah mat, "the king is helpless", and "rook" from rukh, the chariot.
sum: The passage of the Indian board game chaturanga to Sasanian Persia in the 6th century, where it became chatrang. This is the step that set chess on its way west.
